title: Identity Document Review Standards — Claimant Identity Verification
content:
Each identity, address or identity theft document received on a Claimant Identity Verification case is recorded and reviewed, and verification depends on what the accepted documents show.

## Standards

**S1 — Recording.** Each document received is recorded with its type, role and review result.

**S2 — Case status.** A document is recorded only while the case status is opened, in progress or expired; on an expired case only a mailed document whose postmark date is on or before the verification deadline is reviewed. The status and the deadline are taken from the case record before the document is recorded.

**S3 — What verification needs.** Verification needs the pathway's number of accepted primary documents from its accepted primary list and of accepted secondary documents from its accepted secondary list, plus an accepted proof-of-address document from the accepted address list where the pathway requires one.

**S4 — Expiration.** A primary document must be unexpired, except that the pathway's expired-document grace months, counted in calendar months from the expiration date, allow a recently expired one.

**S5 — Proof of address.** A proof-of-address document is accepted only when it shows the mailing address of record and was issued no more than the maximum age in calendar days before it was received.

**S6 — Name differences.** When a document shows a name different from the profile, a legal name-change document is also required.

**S7 — Form and Social Security number.** Documents are accepted only in the pathway's accepted form, and the Social Security number is matched against Social Security Administration records; after an SSA mismatch notice the claimant has the mismatch resolution days to submit the Social Security card or an SSA letter.

**S8 — Resubmission.** A rejected document of a role may be resubmitted no more than the pathway's resubmission limit; reaching the limit without an accepted document of that role fails the case. Resubmissions of a role are counted, over the life of the case, as the documents of that role received after the first rejected one of that role.

**S9 — Authenticity.** A document failing authenticity checks is rejected and referred to the fraud unit.

## Recording by case status (S2)

| Case status | Document recorded and reviewed |
|---|---|
| opened | yes |
| in progress | yes |
| expired | only a mailed document postmarked on or before the verification deadline |
| verified, failed, fraud confirmed or closed | no |

## Conditions for a proof-of-address document (S5)

| Shows the mailing address of record | Issued no more than the maximum age before receipt | Accepted |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | yes |
| yes | no | no |
| no | yes | no |
| no | no | no |

## Worked cases (hypothetical documents and figures)

- **Grace months.** On a pathway with a hypothetical 12-month grace, a driver's license that expired 10 months before it is presented is a recently expired document the grace allows; one that expired 14 months before is not. On a pathway with no grace months, the license must be unexpired.
- **Resubmission count.** On a pathway with a hypothetical resubmission limit of 1, a primary document is rejected; a second primary document then received is 1 resubmission. If that one is also rejected, the limit is reached without an accepted primary document, and the case is failed.
- **Name change.** A passport issued in a former surname that differs from the profile name requires, in addition, a legal name-change document.
- **Expired case, mailed document.** On an expired case whose deadline was 22 March, a mailed document postmarked 21 March is reviewed even though it arrives on 26 March; one postmarked 24 March is not.
